heroSub: Ten low-budget stays in Nan we've reviewed in depth, every one scoring 8.2+ — from cute Old Town dorms under a hundred baht a night and a small boutique near the airport to a rice-field homestay with Doi Phu Kha views, plus riverside bungalows and villas deep in the Bo Kluea valley. Starting from around ฿99–1,200/night.
introH2: 🏔️ Can you do Nan on a small budget — and which area should you base yourself in?
introHtml: Nan is famous for its pretty rice-view and mountain-view resorts, but the town hides far more good-value stays in the low hundreds to low thousands of baht than most people expect — cute Old Town dorms, small owner-run boutiques, homestays out in the rice fields, and bungalows and villas by the streams in the deep valleys. The key to doing Nan on a budget is to match your base to your plans, because Nan's sights are spread far apart — the Old City (Nai Wiang) is the hub, with Wat Phumin, the museum and the walking street, all walkable in a day · Pua district sits about 60 km from town, a zone of stepped rice terraces and the road up Doi Phu Kha · and Bo Kluea lies another ~80 km out, a deep valley of ancient salt wells reached by a winding two-hour mountain road. This guide rounds up 10 budget stays in Nan we've reviewed, every one scoring 8.2 or higher — each from reading real guest reviews, with the honest pros and cons, prices compared on 3 sites, and direct booking links.
mrtHtml: Nan has no metro and very little public transport in town — renting a car or motorbike is by far the most practical option, especially if you head up to Pua or Bo Kluea. In the Old City you'll find a few tuk-tuks and songthaews, but they're hard to flag down in the evening · Nan Nakhon Airport (NNT) is only about 10 minutes from town. The areas in this guide: Old City / Nai Wiang — Wat Phumin, the Nan museum, the walking street, all walkable (CuteinNan, Paknap, Dhevaraj) · Pha Sing / edge of town — quiet, near the airport, best with a car (Muen Chang, Pround) · Phu Phiang — rice views close to town, on the Phra That Chae Haeng road (Chomna) · Pua district — stepped rice terraces, the road up Doi Phu Kha, Wat Phra That Beng Sakkad (Hinpha, PuaDeView) · Bo Kluea — the ancient salt wells, riverside valleys, mountain roads (Tonnam, Boklua River Villa) · for the Pua and Bo Kluea stays a car is strongly recommended, as public transport is scarce and the distances are long.

entries.storyHtml: A riverside stay deep in the Bo Kluea valley on an affordable budget — Tonnam Nan Boklua is a set of minimalist Japanese-style wooden bungalows by the water, from ฿900/night, scoring 8.2 from 64 reviews · The highlight reviewers mention most is the outdoor bathtub off the bedroom, where you soak looking out over the river and mountains, plus riverside seating, a star-gazing tent spot, and pet-friendly rooms — a handy base for the Bo Kluea salt wells, Sapan village, and the road up Doi Phu Kha · The honest caveats: it's about 2 hours from Nan town on a winding mountain road, the bungalows are compact (~20 sqm, right for two), and shops nearby are limited and close early · Best for couples and nature lovers who want to slow down by the water, not those needing full in-town convenience.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Prone to car sickness? Take medication and travel by day, since the mountain road winds for ~2 hours · Buy food and water and fill up in town or Pua before heading up, as shops around Bo Kluea are limited and close early · Want the outdoor-bathtub bungalow? Book ahead and specify the room.

noteHtml: 📌 Note: All prices are approximate starting rates outside the peak season and can change by date and season — always check live prices and compare 3 sites before booking · The scores and highlights here come from reading real guest reviews on the booking platforms; we did not stay in person · Every stay here scores 8.2+, but these are budget 2–3 star properties, so they come with trade-offs — hostels have shared bathrooms, some have no pool, and some sit on the edge of town or out in the districts, not within walking distance of the sights, so please read each stay's caveats before booking · Muen Chang books directly on Agoda, and Hinpha on Agoda and Trip.com — so those two can't be price-compared across all 3 sites, while the other 8 can · Over Nan's cool season (Nov–Jan) and long weekends stays fill fast, especially in Pua and Bo Kluea, so book 1–2 months ahead · Nan has no metro and little public transport, so a rented car or motorbike is easiest, especially for Pua/Bo Kluea · Nan airport is about 10 minutes from town · Article by ThailandAddict.com
faqTitle: FAQ — common traveller questions about budget stays in Nan

faq.q: ❓ What's the best-value budget stay in Nan?
faq.a: By value (score per baht), CuteinNan Hostel from ฿99 a bed, scoring 8.7, is the best value in this set · For a cheap private room, Muen Chang Nan Boutique ฿500 (boutique, 8.9) and Chomna Resort ฿750 (rice-view resort, 9.0) are strong value · The highest score in the set is Hinpha Homestay at 9.3 for ฿900 (breakfast included).

faq.q: ❓ How much do budget stays in Nan cost?
faq.a: In this guide, prices start from around ฿99–1,200 per night · At the cheap end: CuteinNan from ฿99 (dorm bed), Paknap ฿360, Muen Chang ฿500, Chomna ฿750 · On the rice-view / riverside side: Hinpha and Tonnam ฿900, PuaDeView and Pround ฿1,000, Dhevaraj ฿1,100 and Boklua River Villa ฿1,200 · All are approximate starting rates outside peak season; the cool season and long weekends push them up noticeably.

faq.q: ❓ Which area of Nan should I stay in on a budget?
faq.a: It depends where you'll explore — the Old City / Nai Wiang suits temples, the museum and the walking street on foot (CuteinNan, Paknap, Dhevaraj) · Pha Sing / edge of town is near the airport, good for people with a car or an early flight (Muen Chang, Pround) · Phu Phiang gives rice views close to town (Chomna) · Pua district is stepped rice terraces and Doi Phu Kha (Hinpha, PuaDeView) · Bo Kluea is the riverside valley with the ancient salt wells (Tonnam, Boklua River Villa) · Pua and Bo Kluea are far from town, so you need a car.

faq.q: ❓ Do I need a car to do Nan on a budget?
faq.a: For the Old Town only, you can walk or cycle (several stays have free bikes — CuteinNan, Paknap, Dhevaraj, Pround) · But to reach Pua (~60 km from town) or Bo Kluea (~80 km on a winding road, ~2 h), a car is all but essential, as public transport is very limited · The edge-of-town stays like Muen Chang and Pround also suit people with a car · Renting a car or motorbike is the most convenient, flexible option.

faq.q: ❓ Are there budget stays in Nan with a swimming pool?
faq.a: Yes · Dhevaraj Hotel ฿1,100 has an outdoor pool right in the centre of town, rare at this price, and PuaDeView Boutique Resort ฿1,000 in Pua has a mountain-view pool with pool-access rooms · The cheaper stays (hostels/homestays/bungalows) mostly have no pool and lean on location and atmosphere instead.

faq.q: ❓ Which site is cheapest for booking in Nan?
faq.a: Prices on each site (Agoda, Booking.com, Trip.com) vary with each period's promotions, so open and compare all 3 before booking · 8 of the 10 stays here can be compared across all 3 sites (Muen Chang is on Agoda, and Hinpha on Agoda/Trip.com) · Each review page has the full set of price-comparison links, which can save you tens to hundreds of baht a night.
